claims.proposition_evaluated: At its meeting of 2026-08-26 the Infrastructure Committee rejected (a motion to adopt R was put and defeated, or a motion incompatible with R was carried) administration's Recommendation 1 of report IS03688 (R), and R proposed a hold (an express deferral of the routes listed apart under the operative Attachment 5), and no body (the committee or City Council) adopted R by 2026-09-25.
claims.interpretation_notes: Operative version. The minutes of 2026-08-26 (item 1.4) added 'Attachments 2, 3, 5 (Version 1) and 5 (Version 2)' as replacement attachments. Item 7.6 lists all three versions of Attachment 5, and neither the agenda nor the minutes say which one was before the committee when 7.6 was considered. So the operative version is uncertain, and Version 2 (DocumentId 304030) is the declared primary reading. Did R propose a hold? Under Version 2, no, on the primary deferral reading. Version 2 says the remaining routes 'will be evaluated for trade-offs, alternative design treatments and budget implications' and that a Q1 2027 report will outline 'trade-offs and options for the remaining routes ... for Council direction and approval'. The listed projects 'may be re-evaluated using alternate design approaches'. Nothing in the text says these routes wait for that report. Deferral is implied only because they are set against the list that 'will continue as planned'. Under Version 1 (304031) and the original (304032), yes: routes that affect travel lanes or parking 'will be removed', and the original says the listed projects 'would be removed from the scope ... for 2026 and 2027' until re-evaluation. Disposition. At item 7.6 no member moved a motion to adopt R. The only substantive motion was A. Salvador's, which would have continued the programme at its previously approved scope. It was incompatible with R and was defeated 2 to 2. A. Knack and A. Paquette were not in either vote list. The committee therefore left R without a decision as the brief defines it. It did not reject R. What fails in the primary proposition is 'rejected': no motion adopting R was put and defeated, and no incompatible motion carried. Under Version 2, 'hold' also fails. Classification: under both the hold ladder (Version 1 and original) and the no-hold ladder (Version 2) the result is Partially supported, so the verdict does not depend on the version but the reason does. Under Version 2 it is Partially supported because R was not an express hold and was left without a decision. Under Version 1 and the original it is Partially supported because a hold was left without a decision. Alternative reading of 'did not support' (non-adoption alone suffices): Supported, because no body adopted R. The finding is definition-sensitive. Alternative body: in the Council records carried, R and report IS03688 did not come before City Council between 2026-08-26 and 2026-09-25. The only related Council item was a notice of motion (2026-09-08, item 11.6) asking for budget options, laid over to 2026-10-06. For City Council as a body the result is Not established, because it never received R. Override strand: the committee made no decision on R. Its only carried decision at 7.6 kept Attachment 4 private (4 to 0). No later Council decision contradicts anything the committee decided, so the minutes show no override. Reading of the two commenter strands: 'Council chose to ignore' administration's recommendation is borne out only as non-adoption, and by a committee, not Council. 'Ignore a committee's decision' has no committee decision on R to rest on.

Rutherford to delete 'and maximize remaining construction season, including advancing partial and accelerated construction' from Part 2 was also defeated 2 to 2 (in favour Rutherford and Clarke; opposed Salvador and Janz). Stevenson, K. Tang and J. Wright attended but were not committee members.

claims.proposition_evaluated: In report IS03688 for the Infrastructure Committee of 2026-08-26, administration recommended approval of an approach (Attachment 5, operative version) that expressly defers construction or advancement of exactly 14 named route entries of the programme until a further evaluation, report or decision, each of which was unbuilt (construction not started) at the Attachment 3 status date of August 10, 2026.
claims.interpretation_notes: Recommendation 1 asks for approval of the approach in Attachment 5, so that element holds. Operative version: the minutes (item 1.4) add both replacement Versions 1 and 2 without saying which governed at item 7.6. Version 2 (DocumentId 304030) is therefore the declared primary. Count: all three versions list the same 14 entries for re-evaluation and the same 13 entries to 'continue as planned'. Counting by entry, the list is 14. Splitting entries joined by 'and' or commas gives 18: '93 Street ... and 84 Avenue ...' becomes 2, '93 Avenue/82 Street/94 Avenue ... and 75 Street ...' becomes 2, and the Grovenor entry becomes 3. I would not split slash-joined continuous routes. The continue-as-planned list is 14 if '110 Avenue/90 Street ... and 112 Avenue ...' is split. Deferral, Version 2: this fails the primary reading. The text says the remaining routes 'will be evaluated for trade-offs, alternative design treatments and budget implications', that a Q1 2027 report will go 'for Council direction and approval', and that the listed projects 'may be re-evaluated'. It never states that these routes wait for that step. The brief expressly says evaluation for trade-offs or a report back does not qualify without that. Deferral is implied only by contrast with the 'will continue as planned' list. Version 2 also fails the stricter alternative, since it states no removal or 'will not proceed'. Version 1 meets the primary reading: routes 'would be evaluated to determine if they should proceed'. It also meets the stricter reading: routes affecting travel lanes or parking 'will be removed'. The original meets both: the listed projects 'would be removed from the scope ... for 2026 and 2027' pending evaluation. Status: Attachment 3 (304028 and 304029), the primary status record, was not carried and returned HTTP 403, so every route is unresolved at the primary date. At the alternative date, 2026-08-26, Attachment 5 itself is a dated City record. In all versions it limits the approach to routes 'that have not yet started construction'. In the original and Version 1 it describes the continue list as including 'projects that are already under construction'. That places all 14 entries among unstarted routes, but only at document level, not route by route. Classification under Version 2 (primary): Partially supported. What fails is 'expressly defers' (the word 'freezing'). The count of 14 and the recommendation element hold, and unbuilt status is unresolved at the primary date. Under Version 1 and the original: all elements except status hold. At the primary status date that gives Not established, because unresolved status is the only obstacle to Supported. At the alternative status date it gives Supported, if Attachment 5's scope sentence is accepted as establishing unbuilt status. The finding is therefore version-sensitive. The two earlier versions went further than a freeze (removal from scope), and the final version is milder than one. Under Version 2 the report body separately says 'for routes where construction has not yet started, construction is best postponed to 2027', on weather grounds. That sentence applies to all unstarted routes and is not part of the Attachment 5 approach, so I did not treat it as meeting the definition. Qualification 3: the report says the recommendations 'would not result in any changes required to the existing capital profile CM-20-0330 ... or associated borrowing bylaws'. Qualification 4: the recommendation was addressed to Infrastructure Committee to recommend to City Council, with 'Council decision required'.

supporting_evidence.finding: Recommendation 1 asks Infrastructure Committee to recommend to City Council approval of 'the updated approach for the remaining routes ... as outlined in Attachment 5'. claims.suggested_one_line: Administration did single out 14 route entries. Its final version proposed re-evaluating them with a report to Council in early 2027 but did not say in terms that they would wait; earlier versions said they would be removed from the programme.
claims.suggested_short_answer: Report IS03688 recommended an approach listing 14 route entries apart from 13 that would continue as planned, so the number 14 is right. Whether that was a 'freeze' depends on the version. The final replacement (Version 2), which this finding treats as primary because the minutes don't say which version governed, calls for the 14 to be 'evaluated for trade-offs, alternative design treatments and budget implications' with a report to Council in Q1 2027. Final version: re-evaluate plus report in Q1 2027, with no express hold on the routes.
Earlier versions: remove from 2026–27 scope, which is stronger than a freeze.

claims.proposition_evaluated: Between 2022-11-30 and 2026-09-25, Councillors Karen Principe and Jennifer Rice brought (either moved or seconded) two motions at City Council that would each have left capital profile CM-20-0330 with about $50 million (a remainder between $45 million and $55 million of the approved budget at the time), each named a destination for the released funds, and City Council defeated both.
claims.interpretation_notes: Two candidate motions were found. Both were moved by K. Principe and seconded by J. Rice, on separate occasions, at City Council budget meetings, and both were defeated. Motion A is Fall 2023 SCBA Capital Budget Amendment 2 (meeting beginning 2023-11-21; the carried text does not give the exact day of the vote). As restated and put, it read: 'That capital profile CM-20-0330 - Active Transportation Implementation Acceleration - Approach 3 be reduced by $50,000,000 ($16,350,000 in 2024, $16,825,000 in 2025, and $16,825,000 in 2026) with a funding reduction from tax-supported debt'. It was defeated 4 to 8. In favour: S. Hamilton, T. Cartmell, J. Rice, K. Principe. Opposed: A. Knack, A. Paquette, A. Sohi, A. Salvador, K. Tang, E. Rutherford, A. Stevenson, J. Wright. M. Janz is in neither list. As first moved, the text sent the $50,000,000 'to go towards the tax levy'; the restated text replaced this. Motion B is Fall 2024 SCBA Capital Budget Amendment 2 (meeting beginning 2024-12-02): 'That capital profile CM-20-0330 ... be decreased by $33,650,000 in 2025 and $33,650,000 in 2026 with funding from tax-supported debt, to defund planning, design and delivery of the Active Transportation Implementation Acceleration - Approach 3 project'. It was defeated 4 to 7. In favour: T. Cartmell, J. Rice, E. Rutherford, K. Principe. Opposed: A. Knack, A. Sohi, A. Salvador, M. Janz, K. Tang, A. Stevenson, J. Wright. S. Hamilton and A. Paquette (absent with notice) are in neither list. Base: $100,000,000, approved by Capital Budget Amendment 7 as restated and carried 9 to 4 in the 2022 budget deliberations. IS03688 (2026) still describes the programme as '$100 million' approved. I found no approved adjustment changing the total, but I did not read the capital profile attachments. Amount, primary band (reviewer's arithmetic): Motion A leaves $100,000,000 - $50,000,000 = $50,000,000, which meets the band. Motion B cuts $33,650,000 + $33,650,000 = $67,300,000 and leaves $32,700,000, which fails the $45M-$55M band. Alternative band (at least half): Motion A is 50% and meets it; Motion B is 67.3% and meets it. Destination: Motion A's 'with a funding reduction from tax-supported debt' names a reduction in borrowing, so it meets the rule. Motion B names its funding source ('with funding from tax-supported debt') and a purpose ('to defund'). Whether that is a named destination is ambiguous: strictly it states no destination, while read as a debt-funding line it amounts to a reduction in borrowing. What fails in the primary proposition: only one of the two motions (A) would have left about $50 million. Motion B would have left about $32.7 million, a deeper cut than the holder described. The Supported row fails and Partially supported applies (at least one jointly brought reduction motion defeated). Under the co-sponsorship reading the classification is the same, because Principe moved and Rice seconded both. Under the alternative amount band it is Supported if Motion B's tax-supported-debt wording is credited as a destination, and Partially supported if not. The finding is definition-sensitive on the amount band. Qualification 4, other motions: Fall 2023 Capital Budget Amendment 3 (moved Rice, seconded Principe) to reduce $26,808,000 from the 2024 capital budget does not name CM-20-0330 in its text and was withdrawn. City Council 2025-09-16 item 10.13 (moved T. Cartmell, seconded K. Principe), to cease construction on unstarted bike lane projects pending a review, was defeated 4 to 9 (in favour Hamilton, Cartmell, Rice, Principe). That was a pause motion, not a funding reduction. At the 2022 budget, Rice and Principe voted against Capital Budget Amendment 7 but brought no motion on the amount. claims.suggested_one_line: Principe and Rice did twice move to cut the bike-lane programme and lost both times. The first motion would have left $50 million; the second, a $67.3-million cut, would have left about $32.7 million (reviewer's calculation).
claims.suggested_short_answer: Yes, twice, but only one of the two motions was a cut to $50 million. In November 2023, Principe moved and Rice seconded a $50-million reduction to the $100-million programme, with a matching reduction in tax-supported debt; Council defeated it 4–8. In December 2024 the same pair moved to remove the programme's 2025 and 2026 funding, $67.3 million in total. That would have left about $32.7 million (reviewer's calculation), and it was defeated 4–7. If 'cut it to $50M' is read loosely as 'cut it by half or more', both motions qualify.
suggested_tldr: Two separate motions, both moved by Principe and seconded by Rice, both defeated at City Council (2023: 4–8; 2024: 4–7).
2023 motion: cut $50M, leaving $50M, with a funding reduction from tax-supported debt.
2024 motion: cut $67.3M, leaving about $32.7M (reviewer's calculation), which is deeper than 'to $50M'.
The verdict depends on the amount definition: both motions cut at least half.
